schema_evolution.unknown_version_policy: reject: an unrecognized schema_version fails closed rather than being read under v1 semantics
schema_evolution.unknown_field_policy: reject: deserialization denies unknown fields so an execution-significant field can never be silently dropped
schema_evolution.additive_forward_policy: a forward-compatible additive field requires an explicit schema_version increment and its own preserve-or-reject rule
digest_exclusions: incidental JSON formatting, key order, and array order

determinism.normalization_note: The canonical digest is a recursive content walk with byte-ordinal ordering, so identical semantic inputs normalize to identical bytes across map order, locale, clock, checkout path, and retrieval order.
determinism.stable_id_rule: stable_node_id survives issue-title edits and generated projection changes; it is never derived from a title or a live projection

This revision is a schema fixture subset: it proves the contract can express every role, horizon, edge kind, and old-path disposition, and it does not represent the runtime programme graph.
No node here asserts that its proposition is implemented on any tree.
No current, live, observed, or released fact is representable in this contract by construction.

The stack vocabulary carries only the relations the fixtures actually exercise. A restack relation describes candidate history, which belongs to the live-collaboration plane; it is added here only if the stable graph is ever shown to need it.

The canonical digest escapes the backslash and semicolon that terminate its own scalar tokens. Container delimiters are not escaped inside string content; that is safe here because every scalar token is self-terminating and object keys are fixed by the strict field set, but it is a bound of this canonicalization rather than a general guarantee.
